headline: HSC and equivalent exam results published today for over 12.70 lakh examinees
summary: The results for more than 12.70 lakh examinees will be formally announced at 11:00 AM, with students able to check online and via SMS immediately after.
details: The results of this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations, in which over 12.70 lakh examinees participated, are being published today.
The formal announcement will take place at 11:00 AM in the meeting room of the Secondary and Higher Education Division, Ministry of Education.
Immediately after the announcement, examinees can access their results through their educational institutions, designated websites, and SMS services.
Online results can be checked using roll and registration numbers on the websites https://eduboardresults.gov.bd and https://educationboardresults.gov.bd.
Results can also be obtained instantly by sending an SMS to 16140 from any mobile operator, following the prescribed format.

Applications for re-scrutiny or reassessment of answer scripts for dissatisfied students will begin on November 1 and continue until November 7. Detailed instructions will be available on the respective education board websites.

topic: Fourth nuclear fuel shipment for Rooppur unit 2 arrives
headline_marked: [[Fourth nuclear fuel shipment arrives]] for Rooppur’s second unit
headline: Fourth nuclear fuel shipment arrives for Rooppur’s second unit
summary: The crucial consignment marks a significant step towards the commissioning of the second unit of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant, bolstering Bangladesh's long-term energy security.
details: The fourth consignment of nuclear fuel for the second unit of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant has officially arrived in Bangladesh. This delivery is a vital step in the country's ambitious nuclear energy program.
The fuel, essential for generating electricity, reached the plant site in Ishwardi, Pabna, under strict security measures. Its arrival paves the way for the operational readiness of the unit.

The Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant is Bangladesh's first nuclear power project, built with Russian assistance. It aims to significantly contribute to the nation's power grid and reduce reliance on fossil fuels.

Once fully operational, the two units of the plant are expected to generate 2,400 megawatts of electricity. This will play a crucial role in meeting Bangladesh's growing energy demands and supporting economic development.
caption:
Bangladesh's energy future brightens! The fourth nuclear fuel consignment for Rooppur's second unit has officially arrived, marking a major milestone.

The fourth consignment of nuclear fuel for the second unit of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant has officially arrived in Bangladesh. This delivery is a vital step in the country's ambitious nuclear energy program.

The fuel, essential for generating electricity, reached the plant site in Ishwardi, Pabna, under strict security measures. Its arrival paves the way for the operational readiness of the unit.

The Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant is Bangladesh's first nuclear power project, built with Russian assistance. It aims to significantly contribute to the nation's power grid and reduce reliance on fossil fuels.

Once fully operational, the two units of the plant are expected to generate 2,400 megawatts of electricity. This will play a crucial role in meeting Bangladesh's growing energy demands and supporting economic development.
